# intl-t 1.3.3

Plural rules now follow CLDR for every locale. Upgrade every `intl-t` / `@intl-t/*` package to 1.3.3.

## 🌍 Plurals and ordinals follow `Intl.PluralRules` ([#11](https://github.com/nivandres/intl-t/issues/11))

Before, `plural` and `selectordinal` picked branches with fixed numeric thresholds that only fit English. This produced wrong forms such as:

- `12nd` and `23th` for English ordinals;
- `21 товаров` instead of `21 товар` in Russian;
- `22 plików` instead of `22 pliki` in Polish.

ICU-typed messages now resolve like ICU, in this order:

1. An exact match (`=N`), compared with the number itself.
2. The CLDR category of `n - offset` for the message locale.
3. `other`.

`#` prints `n - offset`. Exact matches no longer need expression evaluation.

**Kept for compatibility:**

- `zero` still matches `0` in every locale, as an intl-t extension.
- Guards such as `>1&<10` still work inside typed plurals.
- Messages without a type (`{n, many {…} other {…}}`) keep the extended matching.

**Behaviour change:** typed plurals in English no longer match `two`, `few` or `many`, because CLDR has no such categories in English. Use `=2`, `=3` or guards instead.

## Fixes

- `relative()`: deltas under one second are now formatted in seconds. Before, `in 500 seconds` was printed for half a second; now it is `in 0 seconds`, or `now` with `numeric: "auto"`.
- The `enabledEval: false` option now also turns off evaluation of option guards. Before, only the `INTL_T_DISABLED_EVAL` environment variable did.
- The extended ordinal words `two` and `three` no longer match 12 and 13.

## 🧪 Quality

- The ICU compatibility suite now runs with the locale each test declares. Before, Arabic, Welsh and Russian cases were checked in English.
- New property tests compare every cardinal and ordinal choice with `Intl.PluralRules`, across 10 locales and values from 1 to 200.
